A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same PCA research, despite the changed title and substantial restructuring. The main text, numerical results, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet experiments, including PCA performance, component ablations, cross-architecture evaluations, cropping analyses, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original ImageNet experiments and adds original PCA object-detection results on PASCAL VOC. Table 11 distinguishes the externally reported VPS results from the work's own results.

M1.justification: The specified PCA procedure remains class-balanced easy-sample pruning, combination of whole images, and patch-restricted augmentation with hard-label supervision. v2's 'constrained augmentation' corresponds to v1's patch extraction, and full-dataset selection was already described. The detection evaluation uses the existing AUM option without documenting a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds object detection on PASCAL VOC 2007+2012, extending actual evaluation beyond ImageNet classification (Table 11). v1's discussion of detection through Mosaic augmentation was background material, not a detection experiment.

E2.justification: The principal ImageNet comparator set is unchanged. Targeted additions include TDDS in the pruning-component comparison, published VPS results in the detection comparison, and DUAL, G-VBSM, and DELT in the expanded timing comparison (v2 Tables 10, 11, and 21).

E3.justification: The new detection evaluation introduces VOC 2007+2012 training, VOC 2007 testing, Faster R-CNN-C4 with ResNet-50, and mAP/AP75/AP50 metrics. PCA, Random, and AUM use 1,000 images, while the cited VPS result uses 1,655. Existing ImageNet protocols largely remain; the settings table also changes EDC's reported PatchShuffle setting from enabled to disabled, without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 expands computational analysis with cross-method wall-clock comparisons and revised relabel profiling, and adds TDDS to the pruning-choice ablation. It removes v1's batch-size memory/time study and several NLL/entropy probability and correlation analyses. The RDED augmentation study is substantially reorganized and reinterpreted in Appendix D.9, partly reusing existing results rather than constituting an entirely new experiment.

E5.justification: The main benchmark retains standard deviations from three independent runs. However, v2 omits v1's 100-random-crops count for the retained cropping measurements and the explicit three-run statement accompanying pruning-component results. The new detection table reports uncertainty but gives no run count and displays unavailable VPS uncertainty as NaN; these disclosures do not establish changes in actual repetition counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds detection outcomes, including PCA's 35.99±0.33 mAP with 1,000 images, TDDS-PCA results, and wall-clock measurements. Profiling values and some ablation improvement annotations change. The principal ImageNet benchmark scores remain identical, but v2 Table 24 changes RDED baseline entries and omits v1's SGD RDED+Extract results; its newly claimed gaps are not established as comparable-setting gains.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix A replace Proposition 4.1's empirical-correlation argument with an explicit binary counterexample and distinguish predictive entropy from true conditional entropy. Theorem 4.2 becomes an entropy-crossing existence result under a new compounding assumption, dropping the previous performance inequality. The mutual-information generalization derivation is removed and replaced by a qualified empirical relationship.

C1.justification: The unified benchmark and hard-label PCA remain the central contributions. v2 explicitly claims the first hard-label dataset-compression framework and foregrounds pruning's superiority over distillation and random subsets more categorically. Its abstract also presents hard-label compression as complementary to informative soft labels, refining the earlier emphasis on shifting away from soft labels.

C2.justification: Appendix D.8 changes the explanation of relabeling overhead from disk writing to GPU-to-CPU transfer. Appendix D.9 newly attributes enlarged PCA–RDED gaps specifically to image preparation despite ambiguous optimizer matching. The entropy/generalization relationship gains calibration qualifications, while the standalone limitation about heuristic augmentation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix E specifies RTX3090 versus A100 80GB allocation by batch size and model, and the detection experiment supplies backbone, framework, and dataset-split information. These are disclosures, not evidence of changed hardware for retained experiments. Code access deteriorates: v1 provides an external repository link, whereas v2's GitHub link targets the PDF's first page internally.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dey's soft-label critique, detection-related references, DUAL, and calibration literature, while removing references associated with discarded theoretical arguments. Appendix D.9 expands positioning against RDED. The core literature remains stable, and the formal DD-Ranking citation corresponds to work already mentioned in v1's concurrent-work footnote.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, benchmarking narrative, method explanation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around unification, three benchmark observations, and explicit pruning insights. The theoretical appendix is rebuilt, supplementary sections are reordered, and a compute-resources section is added. This exceeds terminology changes or isolated additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds conceptual diagrams and a detailed PCA pipeline, replacing the simpler patch-extraction illustration. Separate benchmark plots and tables become paired panels, the pruning-rule table is restructured, and new detection and timing tables are introduced. Existing analyses move between the main text and appendices; the appendix image galleries are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer pipeline explanations, an explicit counterexample for Proposition 4.1, hardware disclosures, and detection evidence improve several aspects. However, the new causal comparison has a material inconsistency: v1 Table 7 reports IPC50 SGD results of 42.0 for RDED+Extract and 42.1 for PCA, whereas v2 Table 24 compares 37.7 with 42.1 and attributes the 4.4-point gap to images under supposedly identical conditions. The 37.7 value was assigned to AdamW in v1. These benefits coexist with weakened support for a central attribution claim, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
